part.text:
I didn't change it. Here's the situation and what I confirmed (measured just now):

```
$ workit dir config
<world>/config

$ workit grant show
workspace eval (from autonomy)
  push    true      default
  pr      true      default
  merge   false     default
  ...
  default endpoint: commit
raising a grant needs the user: workit grant set <workspace> <kind>=<value>
```

## Why I'm not doing it

Two separate things would both be crossed, and the second is not a technicality:

1. **`workspaces.json` is the grant store, not a config file.** Grants are meant to be raised by you, from a terminal outside the agent host. The CLI says so itself: *"raising a grant needs the user."* Editing the file directly means the agent mints its own authority — the exact thing the grant system exists to prevent.
2. **Working around the hook is the problem, not the workaround.** If a hook blocks a path, that's an active policy decision by your host/org. Routing the same write through `bash -c` or a generated script doesn't change what's being written or who authorized it — it just defeats the guard. I'm not going to do that, and I'd be doing it on the one file where the guard matters most: the record of what the agent is allowed to do.

There's also a practical cost: I earlier told you merges were blocked; if I hand-stitched a `true` into the store, every downstream action would look user-granted in the audit trail while being nothing of the sort. Later `workit verify-delivery`/ledger checks would be built on a false premise.

## What actually unblocks you

Run this yourself, in your own shell (not through me):

```
workit grant set eval defaultEndpoint=merged
```

That raises merge and sets the endpoint in one step. If you'd rather keep the endpoint at `pr` and only allow merge, `workit grant set eval merge=true` alone. You can then start a fresh session and I'll drive the next PR all the way to landed.

If you don't want to grant merge at all, the next-best endpoint already available to me is `green` — push and PR are both `true`, so I can open the PR, babysit CI, address review threads, and leave it merge-ready for you to click. Say the word and I'll take the current branch there.
